data._THE_FIRST_REFUSAL_2026_11_24: The rule in _the_default_is_to_integrate - take a maker's published facts unless the maker explicitly forbids it - bit for the first time on 2026-11-24, at record 117, and the answer was NO. MOON by Simaudio (simaudio.com) publishes Terms and Conditions of Sale and Use, linked from every page, whose clause 1.6 reserves the content of the site, naming COMPILATIONS OF DATA among the protected material, and prohibits its use, reproduction, distribution, display or transmission without prior written permission. Clause 1.12 separately bars using the site to infringe intellectual property rights. That is not a copyright footer - every site has one of those and the rule was written to ignore them - it is a stated prohibition that names the activity this catalogue performs and the kind of thing it produces. NO MOON RECORD WAS WRITTEN, and none should be until Simaudio is asked and answers. Five models were read and the figures discarded: the 681, 791, 891, 371 and 491 network players. Their pages were worth having, too - the 491's converter is named in prose and the 681/791/891 publish PCM and DSD ceilings - which is the point of recording the refusal rather than quietly skipping the brand: someone will otherwise read those pages again and not know why there is no record. WHAT THIS COSTS AND WHY IT IS STILL RIGHT: one brand of about forty read, and the alternative is a database whose provenance nobody can defend. The licence question for the whole catalogue is still open (see _permission_alone_is_not_enough and the agenda for Bertrand), and a project that cannot show it respected a plain prohibition has already answered it badly. The next step on MOON is _asking_beats_reading: a short request to Simaudio for permission to record their published ceilings with attribution.
data._asking_beats_reading: Manufacturers are the one party with an active interest in these records being right, and they are the only party that can answer the questions that matter. A maker who fills in their own level-3 fields - whether the DSD path is direct, whether DSD is re-converted internally, the real depth of the ladder, the PCM/DSD level offset - gives in one email what no amount of reading gives at all. Measured on the candidate sources below: they reach level 1 and a PARTIAL level 2, and carry dsd_reconverted_to_pcm and dsd_direct for nobody. Scraping a maker's site is legitimate and useful, and it is still the cheap half of the problem.
data._citing_proves_it_does_not_licence_it: READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING ATTRIBUTION SETTLES ANYTHING. Naming the source does not create permission that was never granted. Attribution is a CONDITION of some licences, not a substitute for one: it satisfies CC BY where CC BY applies, and changes nothing where no licence was given. The citation is mandatory here for a different reason, and a good one - it is this catalogue's evidence rule, no claim without a quoted source, which makes a fact checkable and refutable by the next person. That is worth everything and it is not a right to take.
data._how_to_read_a_makers_site: Read robots.txt and the site's terms of use first: a site's terms are a CONTRACTUAL layer that exists whatever the law says about facts, and plenty of them forbid automated extraction. A robots.txt returning 404 is not a prohibition, and not a permission either - it is silence. Prefer the manual or the datasheet PDF: those are published precisely to be read and quoted. Take the fields a record needs, device by device, never the whole catalogue. Rate-limit, and identify the client by a generic name - never by a person's contact details. Record the URL and THE DATE THAT SOURCE WAS READ, per fact: a maker's specification changes with firmware revisions, so a fact without its own date cannot be re-checked. For a bulk take from a named manufacturer, the decision is the project owner's, not a contributor's: it is their exposure.
data._permission_alone_is_not_enough: A yes is not a licence. ODAC republishes its data under CC BY-SA 4.0, so anything taken in bulk must be redistributable UNDER THAT, by whoever we got it from. Which rules out more than people expect: CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA are compatible and carry attribution forward. CC BY-NC is NOT - this catalogue allows commercial use, that is the point of the licence choice. CC BY-ND is NOT, since the data is reshaped on the way in. ODbL is not straightforwardly compatible with an outgoing CC BY-SA and needs advice before it is assumed to be. And an informal permission - an email saying go ahead - usually grants USE and says nothing about onward redistribution under a share-alike licence, which is the only thing we actually need. So the thing to obtain, and to record with the data, is permission to redistribute under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution. Anything less is a fact-by-fact source, like all the others.
data._status: WHAT HAS BEEN TAKEN FROM THESE SOURCES: nothing. Not one field in this catalogue comes from any of them. They are candidates, listed 2026-11-20, each with the column it could actually fill - because breadth is not the question. The question is which column a source can fill, and on what terms we may pass it on.
data._the_browser_reaches_what_a_fetcher_cann: Four confirmations on 2026-11-24: Eversolo (403), Bluesound (429), emmlabs-meitner.com (429 on two tries, both brands) and ifi-audio.com (429 on every product page, including a retry) all refuse an automated fetch and all read first time in a real browser. Denafrips, whose product pages return an empty shell to a fetcher, also renders in a browser - its specifications simply turn out to be images. So a 403 or a 429 is not a source failure: it is an instruction to use a browser. Two mechanics matter when doing so. The specification block is often in a collapsed element invisible to a plain text extraction, so it must be read from the DOM (iFi hides it in #product-specification, Shopify makers in a <details>, Rockna in a hidden tab panel). And any output containing an ampersand, an equals sign or a question mark is blocked as query-string-shaped, so those characters must be replaced before the text is returned - one ampersand in a specification bullet is enough to lose the whole row, and the row lost that way was « Up to 24bit/192kHz & DSD support over all inputs ».
data._the_default_is_to_integrate: THE STANDING RULE, decided 2026-11-24: a fact published by a maker about its own hardware is integrated unless that site carries an EXPLICIT prohibition on using the information. Not a guessed one, not an inferred one - an explicit one. Waiting for permission that nobody needs to give would stall the catalogue while protecting nothing, because a fact is not licensable: there is no permission to obtain for 'the Topping D90 accepts 768 kHz over USB'. THE RULE COVERS FACTS AND STOPS THERE, and the boundary has to be read with it, because it is where someone will over-apply it. Verbatim prose and IMAGES are copyright, not facts, and for copyright silence is not permission - protection is automatic and needs no declaration. So: the figure, yes; the sentence, as a short quotation serving as evidence, which is what every source field here already holds; the logo or the product photograph, no. And the extent rule still applies on top: device by device stays in case one, mirroring a maker's whole catalogue does not, whatever that site's terms say.
data._the_field_none_of_them_has: None of these carries dsd_reconverted_to_pcm or dsd_direct - the two fields that decide whether a consumer sends DSD at all. They come from measurement or from a documented statement about that device, and nothing else. So these sources can carry the catalogue from level 0 to level 1 at scale, and to a PARTIAL level 2. Never to a complete one.
data._the_gap_in_this_file: Measured 2026-11-24: this file lists five candidate sources and records the licence of NONE of them. It reasons about redistribution in the abstract while never stating, per source, what the terms are - which is the one thing that decides whether case TWO or case THREE applies. Every candidate below now carries a `licence` field set to "not established", because that is what is true. It is not filled in with a guess: a licence invented from memory is exactly the kind of fact this catalogue refuses everywhere else, and it would be invented about somebody else's legal position.
data._the_makers_own_pages: THE FOURTH CASE, and the widest one: a manufacturer publishing specifications for its OWN products. This is not a compilation of other people's facts - it is the maker stating facts about hardware it built, on a page it chose to publish. Recording that a given converter accepts 768 kHz over USB, from the maker's own page, is using a fact, and a fact is not protectable. The sui generis right protects the ASSEMBLY of a database, not the facts inside it, so a maker's product page sits in case ONE and not case TWO. IT IS THE EXTENT THAT DECIDES, NOT THE METHOD. Reading a page by hand and reading it with a script are the same act on the same fact. What changes the act is taking a SUBSTANTIAL PART of a collection: a maker's full product catalogue can itself be a database with substantial investment behind it, and mirroring the whole of it is a different thing from looking up the device a contributor actually owns. One fact per device, because someone needed that device, is the shape that stays in case one - and it is the shape every record here already has.
data._three_cases_not_two: LOOKING SOMETHING UP IS NOT THE SAME ACT AS REPUBLISHING A LIST, and there is a third case that the first two hide. ONE: a fact. Reading a public page and recording that a given converter uses a given chip is using a fact, and facts are not protectable. This is what every record here does, one device at a time, with the source named. It needs nobody's permission. TWO: a compilation, taken wholesale. Copying a compiled list into this catalogue and then passing that catalogue on is a different act. A compiled database can be protected in its own right - the European sui generis database right - independently of whether any single fact in it is. Not done, and not to be done. THREE: a compilation we are ALLOWED to take. This is the only door to bulk import, and it is the case worth working on rather than working around. It is also why 'licence to be settled first' on a source below is an invitation to ASK, not a verdict.
data._topping_fully_characterised_2026_11_25: Worth writing down in full, because Topping has about thirty models and every obvious route to them fails. ONE: the website's Specs tab renders EMPTY - not slow, not JavaScript-gated, empty - verified on the D900 and the D90 III SABRE in a real browser, by clicking the tab and by loading ?tab=specs directly with five seconds' wait; document.body.innerText comes back at about 350 characters containing no rate, no DSD and no THD. TWO: the Download tab does give a manual per model, on a separate host (dl.topping.audio) with unguessable filenames - d90iii_sabre.pdf for the page slug d90-iii-sabre, and D70_Pro_OCTO_V1.2.pdf behind a page slug Topping itself misspells d70-pro-otco-user-manual - so each PDF must be found through its own download page. THREE, and this is the wall: of eight manuals downloaded, SIX HAVE NO TEXT LAYER AT ALL. pdftotext returns exactly one character per page, which is what a PDF made of page images returns. Only DX1_II_V1.2_EN.pdf and E50_II_V1.2_EN.pdf carry text, and their filenames say why - they are the newest products and the only ones with a separate English manual. FOUR: the six image-only manuals probed (D50 III, D90 III SABRE) have no English section whatever; they run Chinese then Japanese. SO THE FIGURES EXIST ONLY AS PHOTOGRAPHED CHINESE TABLES, and reading them would stack a visual transcription on top of a translation. That was declined, for the same reason Denafrips's single specification image was declined the same night: a number read off a picture at speed, with no second reader, is how a wrong figure enters a database that has spent two days refusing inferences far safer than that. The route, if these thirty models are wanted, is to ask Topping for the English manuals or a data sheet. NOTE ON PERMISSION: toppingaudio.com has NO terms-of-use page - 23 internal links, none legal, and a footer reading « (c) 2026 TOPPING Technology co., LTD. All rights reserved. » with Chinese ICP registration numbers. That is the ordinary copyright footer, so nothing here was refused on licence grounds. The two records written are the whole of what Topping publishes in a form that can be quoted.
data._what_a_prohibition_looks_like_against_w: Worth separating, because 40 makers' pages have now been read and 39 of them have footers that say nothing. A FOOTER is « (c) 2026 Maker. All rights reserved. » - an assertion of copyright in the page, which is true of every page on the web and bears on copying the PAGE, not on recording a fact it states. A PROHIBITION names the act: use, reproduction, extraction, compilation, or republication of the data, with or without permission language. Simaudio's clause 1.6 is the second kind. Berkeley's « Copyright (c) 2026, All Rights Reserved - Berkeley Audio Design, LLC » is the first, and its facts are recorded. Where only a terms page MIGHT contain one and was not read, the record says so rather than implying a check that did not happen - several claims written tonight carry exactly that caveat.
data._when_a_maker_has_NO_reachable_publicati: A third case beside « allowed » and « forbidden »: makers whose own site cannot be read at all, so that no datasheet-weight claim about them can ever exist. Measured 2026-11-24 across about forty brands. HOLO AUDIO is the extreme: holoaudio.com returns a 302 to a domain-sale profile at hugedomains.com, so a brand whose whole argument is its discrete R2R design has no maker publication on the web at all. Its three records - May, Spring 3, Cyan 2 - therefore rest on an import (weight 15) and cannot be improved except through a dealer (35) or a measurement (90). LAMPIZATOR is the same shape for a different reason: lampizator.eu serves a certificate belonging to its host's wildcard, which is a misconfiguration and so permanent until they fix it, and what reads instead is a regional site with unfilled template text. EVERSOLO returns 403 to every automated fetch. GUSTARD and SHANLING publish their specifications as images; DENAFRIPS publishes one image per model behind JavaScript; TOPPING renders an empty Specs panel even in a real browser and puts the figures only in per-model PDF manuals. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE CATALOGUE: a record's weight is not a judgement on the maker's honesty, it is a measure of what the maker made reachable. Six brands can never reach datasheet weight as things stand, and the honest response is to say so on the record rather than to promote a dealer's page to datasheet because no better source exists. The route for all six is the same and it is not scraping: ask them. See _asking_beats_reading.

data: Seeded 2026-11-19 from published manuals, maker documentation and public forum threads. Every entry carries its own source; nothing was taken in bulk from anyone's compiled list.

All five makers above put optical at 192 kHz, and interfaces.json still assumes 96 for a device that has not said. That is deliberate. The failure modes are not symmetric: assuming 96 on a 192-capable input costs the listener one rate step they will never notice, while assuming 192 on a 96-capable one costs a device that does not lock and a zone that plays nothing. Five devices in one class is also a thin basis for a default that must hold for every device nobody has checked. The right fix is not a braver default - it is filling the per-device values, which is what the block above does.

open_doubt.text: This is not a standalone converter. Accuphase's own page describes the DAC-50 as an OPTION BOARD that installs in a rear slot of a supported component, so the device a listener actually owns is the host amplifier or player, and that is what the driver will name. The record is kept because its chip-level facts hold, but it cannot be matched by a model name a listener would recognise, and its inputs belong to the host. The inverse of the RME and Schiit case: there a model name covered several devices, here a model name is a part of one.

data.chip: No part number. « Paralleled Flagship DAC devices working in Mono DSD-only mode and special Class-A operation we have developed » - bought silicon, unnamed, several per channel, run in a DSD-only mode. The « transformer-coupled Class-A output stage » is the analogue stage, not the converter, and the maker is explicit that the device is « all-solid-state »: there is no tube here.

device_settings.why: « Proprietary 48 bit PCM to DSD converter module with DSD128 and DSD256 capabilities, user selectable from the remote. » Every PCM input is converted to DSD before conversion, and the owner chooses the rate it is converted TO. DSD256 is the higher of the two the maker offers. This is the first setting in the catalogue that chooses the TARGET of a mandatory internal conversion rather than a filter or a mode - and the only one an engine must read before deciding what to send, because it fixes what the conversion stage will actually see.

S/PDIF, AES/EBU and Optical accepting up to 192kHz/24bit PCM. »; « Two Proprietary DTR inputs allowing connection to DTR-MR and DNP-SR. »; « Proprietary DTR balanced I2S inputs for connecting our digital sources. »; « Note! Both 44.1kHz and 48kHz base frequencies are accepted for DSD. » Also: « Attenuator offering a non-decimating volume control with a 0.5dB step. »; « Ultra-low-phase noise, Femto -jitter Master Clocks. » Self-description: « Pure DSD all-solid-state Digital to Analog converter with a transformer-coupled Class-A output stage. »; « The DSD-WR is our current Reference all-solid-state Digital to Analog converter. »; « The DSD-WR is the final Special Edition for this model. » The page's description also says « From the quadruple DSD processing rate, to the transformer-coupled Class A output stage ».

data._why_the_series_3_is_an_edition_and_not_: The maker's own page carries the Series 3 text inside the 3P page and says the Series 3 « can be fully upgraded to an Alpha DAC Reference Series 3P ». Two names, one upgradable object, and no fact on the page distinguishes them: that is the definition of `edition` here, not of `neighbour`. If a fact ever separates them - a rate, a filter, a converter - the edition becomes a record of its own.

data.chip: A dual-converter design: a commercial AD1955 on the PCM side and a separate discrete implementation for DSD, which is why its family is the discrete DSD architecture rather than a chip vendor.

data.chip: « Dual ESS9038 » from the product description, with « each DAC chip is independently powered and handles only one channel » - two converters in dual mono. The part is named only in the description, never in a specification row, and « ESS9038 » without a suffix does not distinguish an ES9038PRO from an ES9038Q2M.

data.chip: « Dual ESS ES9028Q2M DACs », from the page's own « DIGITAL TO ANALOGUE CONVERTERS » row.

device_settings.why: « Selectable, Fast - Slow - Short delay » - three filters, NAMED, in a specification row. The third is the one to prefer: a short-delay (minimum-phase) response puts the filter's ringing energy after the impulse rather than before it, and pre-ringing is the artefact apodising filters exist to remove - the same reasoning as Rockna's « hybrid phase ». The names are the ES9028Q2M's own filter menu exposed to the user, which is the first time in this catalogue a maker has done that instead of hiding it.

data.chip: No part number, and none to expect: « four precision R-2R converter networks per channel, with all resistors mounted on a common silicon substrate » - eight networks in a dual-mono device, built rather than bought. data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

open_doubt.a_contradiction_to_settle: This doubt says the internal_bypass threshold is the QUTEST's, read from that model's manual. But the claim's internal_bypass carries its OWN source, the brand-level forum sentence above. One of the two is wrong, and it matters because this doubt also says the bypass rate is the figure to check first, since it is the one that changes an answer. Not acted on: measured and written down.
open_doubt.device_level_outcome: KEPT, after checking each field against this record's own quote rather than by analogy with the per-input withdrawal. The quote reads « passing 705.6/768k PCM to a Chord DAC bypasses the built-in WTA1 stage » - it names the rate AND it names the subject at brand level, which is exactly what this catch-all is. So pcm_max_hz: 768000 is supported here, unlike iFi's and MSB's, and `dsd_max` was already "unknown". Removing it for symmetry with the other records would have thrown away a fact its evidence carries.
evidence_kept: Chord Qutest user manual, read 2026-11-20: USB type B 32-bit/768 kHz PCM and up to DSD512; two BNC coaxial at 24-bit/384 kHz, reaching 768 kHz only in the dual-data mode that pairs with the maker's own upscaler; optical 24-bit/192 kHz, DSD64.

SENTENCE WORTH KEEPING, and the reason this is written down rather than deleted: several retailer listings give the Qutest's optical input as 96 kHz, where the manual says 192. Whoever opens a per-model Qutest record will meet that contradiction again, and this is where the answer already is - the manual was the figure taken.
open_doubt.resolution: The per-input ceilings were WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-24. This record's `model` is "unknown" - it is the brand's catch-all, standing for the Qutest, the Hugo, the Dave and the Mojo at once - and per-input ceilings cannot be true of all of them. The claim's own source said whose they were: the Qutest user manual. Keeping them meant asserting one model's inputs for four devices, which is the over-reach this doubt already named.
open_doubt.text: This is the brand's catch-all, and its per-input ceilings and its internal_bypass threshold are the QUTEST's, read from that model's manual. They are asserted here for the Hugo, the Dave and the Mojo as well, on evidence that names only one of them - the same over-reach the iFi record writes down. The rate at which the WTA1 stage steps aside is the figure to check first, since it is the one that changes an answer.
open_doubt.what_remains_unsupported: native_dsd: false and dop: true are not in the quote. They are not an over-reach but an instance of this import batch's known defect - one citation for ten facts - and they belong to the per-field evidence work, not to this withdrawal.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: A per-model record (chord/qutest) carrying these ceilings with this same manual as its source. The figures are not wrong; the subject they were attached to was.

data.chip: No converter chip, by design: « Chord Electronics custom coded Xilinx Artix 7 (XC7A15T) FPGA » driving a « 10 element pulse array design ». The FPGA runs the filter - « Tap-length: 49,152 » - and the pulse array does the conversion.

device_settings.why: Four filters, NAMED, in a user-options block: « Incisive neutral (Ultimate reference) (White) », « Incisive neutral HF roll-off (Green) », « Warm ('Smooth') (Orange) », « Warmer HF roll-off (Red) ». The first is the one to prefer and the maker says why in its own label - « Ultimate reference ». The other three are deliberate departures: two roll off the high frequencies, two are voiced « warm ». Auto's job is to deliver the signal intact and let nothing colour it, so the reference filter is the setting.

data.chip: No converter chip: « Xilinx Artix 7 FPGA, custom-coded by Chord Electronics' Rob Watts » with « 86x 208MHz cores running in parallel », running « advanced 16FS WTA 1 filter with 98,304-taps » into « a 10-element design » pulse array. Twice the tap length of the Hugo 2's 49,152.

device_settings.why: « four-stage user-selectable filter controls » - a count and no names, on a page that gives the tap length to five significant figures. The Hugo 2's page names its four; this one does not. No value can be recorded, and the Hugo 2's names must NOT be copied across: two models of one maker with the same filter COUNT is not evidence that the filters are the same.

source.quote: Chord Electronics' own page for the Hugo TT 2, read 2026-11-24. « Connectivity (input): 1x USB Type-B, 2x Coax BNC & 2x Optical ». One block for all inputs: « PCM support: 44.1kHz, 48kHz, 88.2kHz, 96kHz, 176.4kHz, 192kHz, 352.8kHz, 384kHz, 717.6kHz, and 768kHz. 16 - 32bit ». DSD: « DoP DSD 64 to DSD 512 - native via Windows ». Filters: « four-stage user-selectable filter controls » and « three-stage user-selectable digital crossfeed », with no filter named. Digital output: « 2x DX BNC (expansion outputs) ». Self-description: « DAC, preamplifier & headphone amplifier ». A terms-of-use page was not opened and none of the pages read carries a prohibition.

data.chip: No converter chip and no part number for the FPGA either: « entirely engineered around a powerful, custom-coded FPGA processor », with « Improved WTA filtering: 40 DSP cores ». Neither the Xilinx part nor a tap length is given, unlike the Hugo 2 and the Hugo TT 2.

source.quote: Chord Electronics' own page for the Mojo 2, read 2026-11-24. Inputs: « Five digital inputs: coaxial, dual-data coax, optical, Micro-USB and USB-C » - with no rate or bit depth printed per input. Feature list: « 768kHz Micro USB Input »; « 768kHz Coax Input via Jack »; « 96kHz Optical Input ». DSD: « Up to DSD 256 (4x) Capable » and « DSD via DoP ». Conversion: « entirely engineered around a powerful, custom-coded FPGA processor »; « Improved WTA filtering: 40 DSP cores for better transparency and lower noise »; the marketing page adds « Unique FPGA technology » and « Improved FPGA: more resolution, power and efficiency ». « UHD DSP » is described as « advanced 'digital tone control' ». Menu options: « mute, crossfeed, button-lock, switchable USB-C charging and tone control adjustment ». Self-description: « Class-leading portable DAC/headphone amplifier. » A terms-of-use page was not opened and none of the pages read carries a prohibition.

data.chip: No commercial converter: « Chord Electronics custom coded Xilinx Artix 7 (XC7A15T) FPGA », with « Tap-length: 49,152 » and a « 10 element pulse array design ». The maker's own design, which is why chord_wta exists as a family - and the case the chip model calls « no commercial chip »: a technology stated, no part number to give.

open_doubt.text: Chord publishes TWO different ceilings for this device's optical input: 96 kHz on the product page (stated twice, in the spec table and in the Key Features list) and 192 kHz in the Qutest User manual 2.1. Both claims are recorded. The build resolves by source weight, which puts the page (datasheet, 70) above the manual (65) and therefore lands on the conservative 96 - defensible, and not the same as knowing. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the device itself. An optical input is the one ceiling a probe establishes for free, and this is a clean example of why level 2 is worth collecting even where a maker has published something.

data._why_the_da2_is_a_neighbour_and_not_an_e: The page is explicit that they are different products: « The DA2i builds on the DA2's strengths with noticeable improvements in resolution, timing, and control. » A customer testimonial on the same page writes « The DA2i / DA2 V3 », which suggests the DA2 reached a third revision. Facts DO distinguish them - the maker says so - and the DA2 has no record here, so the name resolves to this one for want of its own. That is `neighbour`, the relation that says « a DIFFERENT product, resolved here ». No figure on this record may be read as the DA2's.
data.chip: No part number, and none exists: « Next generation 16xDSD proprietary discrete dual differential D-to-A converters (MDAC2) », « in-house DACs », « proprietary Dual Differential DACs ». The maker states the stage's own rate - « our flagship 16xDSD (DSD1024) converter » - and that is the rate it RUNS AT, not the rate it accepts. « a newly designed Class A analog output stage » is the analogue stage. MDAT2 is the DSP ahead of the converters, MFAST the frequency acquisition, MCLK3 the clock.

open_doubt.text: Whether this device reconverts incoming PCM to DSD, and at what rate. The shape is unmistakable and the page will not say it. The converters are « 16xDSD » and « MDAT2 DSP works in harmony with the 16xDSD DACs, processing audio in real-time » - a discrete stage that runs at DSD1024 with a DSP in front of it, fed inputs that top out at 24/192 PCM and DSD128. Something upstream must be taking 192 kHz PCM to DSD1024, and pcm_reconverted_to_dsd would be the field for it. The page never states it. Nagra says it in one sentence (« Every input signal is converted into DSD 256 format ») and APL HiFi in another (« All PCM rates from the digital sources are converted to DSD, prior to D/A conversion »), both recorded today; this maker, whose founder built the first DSD systems, says only that its DSP works « in harmony with » the DACs. No fact is written. The inference is strong, which is the reason to be careful rather than a reason to proceed.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: The DA2i brochure or manual, both linked from the product page and neither read. Failing that, one sentence from EMM Labs. Do NOT resolve it from the sister MA3i page, which carries the same bullets and says no more, nor from the architecture: a 16xDSD stage is evidence of what the stage does, not of what happens to the signal before it.

data.chip: DUAL MONO: an AK4191 modulator with an AK4499 converter PER CHANNEL, as the maker's table says twice - « Left Channel: AK4191+AK4499 », « Right Channel: AK4191+AK4499 ». Four AKM parts in two roles. The third record in this catalogue on the AK4191+AK4499 pairing, after gustard/a26 and eversolo/dmp-a8, and the clearest argument yet that a chip model needs a role AND a count per part: « AKM » says nothing about whether a modulator is shared or doubled.

open_doubt.text: `kind` CANNOT SAY WHAT THIS DEVICE IS. It is filed as network_player, in the maker's own words - the page heads it « DMP Streamer Series - DMP-A8 » - and it is equally a USB DAC: the same table lists a USB-B Audio INPUT taking DSD512 and 768 kHz 32-bit from a computer. The field holds one value out of dac and network_player, and this device is both. This is the FIRST record of the population pass and it broke the field immediately, which is worth more than the record: the installed base is full of streamers with a DAC inside and a USB input on the back, and they will all land on this. Picking one value quietly would hide it. Either `kind` becomes a list, or it is renamed to say what it actually answers - how the device is REACHED - and a separate field says whether it converts.

open_doubt.text: How many selectable digital filters does this device have? Ferrum's own two pages give four different answers: « two included at launch », « three filter settings », « four digital filters created for Ferrum by Signalyst », and « One is a part of the ESS DAC, and four were designed especially for WANDLA ». The readings are not even consistent in kind - some count ESS's, some Signalyst's, some both. It matters because selectable filters are a level-3 fact: which one is active changes what the device does to the signal, and a consumer that upsamples needs to know whether its own work will be filtered again. One email to Ferrum settles it.

device_settings.why: « Oversampling setting: OS/NOS ». A two-position switch, stated as a specification row rather than buried in copy. In OS the device applies its own oversampling; in NOS it runs at the rate it is given. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's stage belongs out of the path. This is also what makes correctable true: the field applies « only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM ».

data.chip: Three parts, each with the role its maker gives it: TWO AK4493SEQ converters (AKM), one per channel - « The left and right channels are each equipped with an efficient high-performance AK4493SEQ » - an XMOS XUF208 as the USB interface, called « Decoder » by FiiO, and a « Dual THX AAA 788+ » amplifier stage. device_settings.why: The row « All to DSD » is supported and optional. Left OFF: Auto's whole purpose is to choose the format and rate reaching the conversion stage, and a device-side conversion to DSD would redo that work with a resampler we did not design and cannot account for. Turn it on only for a listener who prefers it and is not using Auto.

data._corrected: Filed under AKM until 2026-11-20 with no source naming any chip. It is ESS. The kernel's quirk table had said so all along - vendor 0x292b is commented "Gustard/Ess based devices" - and that comment was dismissed here as too vague to overturn a record. It was not vague; the record was unsourced. The two Gustard records now sit on two different families, which is why this brand carries none.

open_doubt.device_level_kept: family, dsd_direct, analog_filter and correctable stay: the quote reaches the chip and its DSD behaviour, which is exactly what it talks about.
open_doubt.device_level_resolution: The DEVICE-level ceilings went the same way as the per-input ones, and for a reason that needs no judgement: this claim's quoted source carries NO figure at all - it reads « All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset » and « TI/BB DAC chips only support bit-perfect DSD playback ». It supports a chip family and a DSD behaviour, and nothing about a rate. The figures it was carrying (768 kHz, DSD512) were the Pro iDSD's, as the withdrawn per-input claim said in its own words. Withdrawing the per-input ceilings and keeping the device-level ones would have left the record LOOKING reviewed while still asserting one model's rates for the range.
evidence_kept: iFi Pro iDSD manual, read 2026-11-20, which states it plainly: « Inputs other than USB are currently limited to maximum sample rates of 192kHz PCM and DSD64 via DoP », against USB at 768 kHz and DSD1024.
open_doubt.resolution: The per-input ceilings were WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-24, on the claim's own confession: its source ended with « This record is the range's catch-all and the figures are the Pro iDSD's; the Neo and micro models were not documented per input. » A source that says it does not cover the subject is evidence against the claim it carries.
open_doubt.text: The family here is read from a conditional sentence: "All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset" describes the ones that use that silicon rather than claiming the range does. This record is the brand's catch-all, so it asserts the chip for every iFi converter on evidence that does not go that far.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: A per-model record (ifi/pro-idsd) carrying them. The quoted sentence is unusually clean evidence and should not be lost on the way.

device_settings.why: FIVE filters, all NAMED, in a specification row: « Bit-Perfect/Bit-Perfect+/Gibbs Transient Optimised/Apodising/Transient Aligned ». Bit-Perfect is the one to prefer and the name says why - it is the setting that applies no interpolation of the device's own, which is what Auto needs when it has already chosen the rate and the filter. The other four are real choices and worth knowing: « Gibbs Transient Optimised » targets the overshoot a brick-wall filter produces, « Apodising » is the designed-to-discard-the-source's-own-ringing family, and « Transient Aligned » is the same idea as Chord's WTA. This is the most filter choice any record in the catalogue offers.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

device_settings.why: In OS mode this converter oversamples EVERYTHING by sixteen to 705.6 or 768 kHz with its own filter. In NOS mode it runs at the rate it is given and applies none. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's own stage should be out of the path - the same reasoning as the rate threshold that bypasses Chord's interpolation stage, reached here by a front-panel setting instead of by a rate.

device_settings.why: « Native Zero Upsampling, Zero Oversampling Processing » is a design principle here, not a switch: there is nothing to turn off. That is the precondition `correctable` requires, met by construction rather than by a menu - the first such case in the catalogue, where the other six NOS devices all offer it as a setting.

device_settings.why: The page offers « DSD256 upsampling option for all files » and « PCM 384kHz upsampling option for all files », and « Upsampling and downsampling to every supported format up to DSD256/PCM384 ». Left OFF: Auto's whole purpose is to choose the format and rate reaching the conversion stage, and a device-side resampler would redo that work with a filter we did not design and cannot account for. Turn it on only for a listener who prefers it and is not using Auto. Same reasoning as FiiO's « All to DSD ».

data.chip: No part number: « DAC Circuit New MMM-Conversion », Marantz's own name for its conversion stage, with « MMM-Stream » as the processing ahead of it.

device_settings.why: Four options, named: « Balanced, Natural, Dynamic Music, Dymanic Voice ». « Balanced » is the one to prefer - the other three are voicings aimed at material types, and Auto's job is to deliver the signal rather than to characterise it. The page also offers « Filter 1, 2 Selectable » and « Dither 1, 2, Off », whose effects it never describes, so no value is recorded for those two.

data._kind_is_wrong_here_and_there_is_no_righ: The maker calls it « a streaming preamplifier that unites analog with digital ». It streams over network and Wi-Fi, converts, preamplifies, and carries « 6 analog inputs ... plus 1 dedicated phono input for turntables ». kind takes one value and this catalogue knows two: dac and network_player. `dac` is recorded because the conversion stage is what this database is FOR, and the record therefore says nothing about the streaming half, the analogue half or the phono stage. Sharpest case yet of a gap already noted: kind is a single value where makers build one box that is three things.
data.chip: No part number and no maker. « 8-channel, 32-bit/384kHz PCM/DSD, Quad Balanced » - eight converter channels serving two output channels, four per side in a balanced arrangement. The page never says whose silicon it is, nor whether it is bought, discrete or an FPGA.

source.quote: McIntosh's own page for the CS7500, read 2026-11-24. Spec table, Digital Audio Specifications: « Digital Coaxial Input Sample Rate » = « 24-bit/44.1kHz to 192kHz »; « Digital Optical Input Sample Rate » = « 24-bit/44.1kHz to 192kHz »; « Digital MCT Input Sample Rate » = « 16-bit/44.1kHz (CD) » and « DSD64 (SACD) »; « Digital USB Input Sample Rate » = « 32-bit/44.1kHz to 384kHz (PCM) » and « DSD64, DSD128, DSD256, DSD512, DXD352.8kHz, DXD384kHz »; « Digital Network/Wi-Fi Input Sample Rate » = « 24-bit/44.1kHz to 192kHz ». Connectivity: « Digital Coaxial Input » = « 2 »; « Digital Optical Input » = « 2 »; « Digital MCT Input » = « 1 »; « Digital USB Input » = « 1 »; « HDMI (ARC) Input » = « 1 ». Body: « The CS7500 features 6 analog inputs consisting of 2 balanced, 3 unbalanced, 1 dedicated phono input for turntables, plus 7 digital audio inputs. »; « the USB input supports native DSD512 and DXD up to 384kHz »; « the coaxial and optical inputs handle up to 24-bit / 192kHz »; « The HDMI (ARC) input will only play audio from a compatible TV. » Converter: « Quad Balanced 8-channel, 32-bit DAC » and the spec row « Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) Type » = « 8-channel, 32-bit/384kHz PCM/DSD, Quad Balanced », with « This next-generation, Quad Balanced, 8-channel, 32-bit architecture ». Self-description: « a streaming preamplifier that unites analog with digital while elevating both » and « State-of-the-art streaming and expert preamplification in one uncompromising component ».

data.chip: No part number, and none exists: « Next generation 16xDSD proprietary discrete dual differential D-to-A converters (MDAC2) », built in-house. MDAT2 is the signal processing ahead of them, MFAST the frequency acquisition, MCLK3 the clock, VControl the volume - four named blocks and not one bought part.

open_doubt.device_level_outcome: KEPT for now, and the reason is not that the figures are doubtful - the quote names « up to 384/24 and DSD256 » for one Merging Hapi, so they are supported. The defect is the SUBJECT, not the number: this record stands for every generation and every fitted card under one model name. Withdrawing the figures would lose true facts about a real unit. The fix is to key records by generation and card, which this doubt has asked for since 2026-11-20, and it is an identity question rather than a withdrawal.
evidence_kept: Merging Hapi MkII specifications, read 2026-11-20: 44.1 to 384 kHz PCM plus DSD64, DSD128 and DSD256 over the network.
open_doubt.resolution: The per-input ceiling was WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-24. The Hapi is MODULAR: its ceilings follow the card fitted, not the model name, so a single figure under the model is a claim the hardware does not support. The claim's own source named the generation it came from - the MkII specifications - while this doubt records that the MkIII's standard cards stop at 192 kHz.
open_doubt.text: The Hapi is MODULAR and its ceilings follow the card fitted, not the model name: on the MkIII the standard I/O cards stop at 192 kHz while the premium card reaches 352.8 and 384 kHz with DSD256. The figure recorded here is the MkII's. Third device in this catalogue whose model name does not determine its capability, after MSB's plug-in USB modules and the variants of the RME ADI-2 and the Schiit Yggdrasil.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: Records keyed by generation and fitted card, not by model name. Same shape as MSB's plug-in USB modules and the Schiit Yggdrasil variants, which this doubt already lists.

data.chip: No part number, and the maker says why: « We decided to design, from the ground up, a discrete DAC » with « circuits and digital algorithms that were entirely developed in house ». The stage is « a discrete 32-stage FIR DAC and a single-stage 4th order filtering I/V converter », fed noise-shaped PWM at 3.125 MHz/32 bits.

source.quote: Mola Mola's own page for the Tambaqui, read 2026-11-24. OPERATING PRINCIPLE: « PWM DAC with 32-stage discrete analogue FIR output stage. Avoids 'sigma delta' tones and 'R2R' glitch and low-level linearity errors. » and « Asynchronous upsampling to 3.125MHz/32 bit. 7-th order noise shaper clearing 80kHz band. Each input rate has an optimized upsampling filter chain. » SUPPORTED FORMATS: « PCM up to 384kHz/32 bits (>192kHz and >24 bits via USB and Roon only) » and « DoP and Native DSD up to quad speed (USB and Roon only) ». I/O: « Optical (Toslink) », « S/PDIF (Cinch) », « AES/EBU (XLR) », « USB type B », « Ethernet (Roon Ready) », « Bluetooth (SBC, AAC, APTX, LDAC) », « IBIS over HDMI », « Balanced output (XLR) », « Headphone output (6.3mm Jack, Balanced XLR 4pin) ». PERFORMANCE: « Signal to Noise Ratio: 130dB »; « THD, IMD: not measurable (estimated -140dB) »; « Bandwidth: Up to 80kHz (apodizing response) »; « Integrated jitter: <1ps from 10Hz upwards, <300fs from 1kHz upwards ». Body text: « The converter is a two board stack. On the first board, all incoming digital audio is upsampled to 3.125MHz/32 bits and converted to noise shaped PWM. On the other board are two mono DACs, in which a discrete 32-stage FIR DAC and a single-stage 4th order filtering I/V converter, convert the PWM into analogue with a breathtaking 130dB SNR. This is near the theoretical limit for 24-bit files and far beyond that of even quad-speed DSD. »; « With the addition of a lossless digital volume control and headphone outputs »; « The Mola Mola Tambaqui is Roon Ready certified! »; « Responding to popular demand, Mola Mola launched the famous discrete DAC from the Makua as a separate unit. » The companion page https://www.mola-mola.nl/dac.php adds: « We decided to design, from the ground up, a discrete DAC »; « circuits and digital algorithms that were entirely developed in house »; and that the same two-board converter « fits into one of the option slots in the preamp ». Self-description: « Tambaqui - the DAC that Stands Alone ».

open_doubt.device_level_kept: family and the ladder description stay - that is what the sentence actually says. dsd_direct was already `to_be_measured`.
open_doubt.device_level_resolution: The whole of this record's evidence is one sentence - « it is an R2R DAC (and thus native PCM) » - and it names no rate, no DSD format and no transport. It carried 768 kHz and DSD256 anyway. This doubt already said no per-input figure would be true of every unit sold under this name, because the USB input is a plug-in card; the same is true of a device-level figure, which is why none is left. Nothing here needed a judgement about over-reach: the evidence rule alone disposes of it.
open_doubt.text: MSB converters are MODULAR: the USB input is a plug-in card, so a given unit's ceiling depends on which module is fitted rather than on the model name. A review of the Discrete describes one with 768 kHz and DSD512 over USB while the fixed coaxial, optical and XLR inputs sit far lower. No per-input figure is recorded here because none would be true of every unit sold under this name - a third shape of the same problem, after a model that spans chips and a model that is a part.

open_doubt.text: What performs the conversion. The page names « A high-performance FPGA » for « all internal calculations » and « two NOS military JAN5963 tubes » for the output, and nothing in between. Every input becomes DSD256, so something turns a 1-bit stream at 11.2 MHz into analogue, and the page does not say what. technology was briefly recorded as fpga and withdrawn (see the claim's own note): Rockna demonstrates on one device that an FPGA can do all the digital work while a discrete ladder converts.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: The Nagra HD DAC X user manual, linked from the product page and not read. Do NOT resolve it from « performs all internal calculations »: that sentence has now been shown, on another maker's page, to be compatible with a separate conversion stage.

device_settings.why: « High Quality optionally selectable upsampling of PCM and/or MQA content with propriatory filtering ». Optional and the owner's choice, so left off for the same reason as LUMIN's and FiiO's: Auto has already chosen the rate and designed the filter, and a device-side resampler with a proprietary filter would redo that work with something we cannot account for.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.

data._two_editions_the_schema_cannot_tell_apa: One page, two products: « RD-0 (used in Signature - 27 bit structure) and RD-1 (used in Edition - 26 bit structure) », with two output blocks measuring 132 dB and 122 dB SNR. Facts DO distinguish them, so `edition` is a stretch - and every field this catalogue HOLDS is identical for both: same inputs, same rates, same filters, same NOS switch, same ladder topology. What separates them is the module's bit structure, THD, SNR and output voltage, none of which the schema has. So the two names resolve here, as editions, and the reason is recorded: not missing evidence, but evidence about things the catalogue does not model.
data.chip: No part number, because the modules are the maker's own: « dedicated dac modules called RD-0 (used in Signature - 27 bit structure) and RD-1 (used in Edition - 26 bit structure) ... sharing a discrete sign-magnitude hybrid ladder topology, driven by a complex algorythm which is embedded into their own FPGA ». TWO FPGAs, doing two different jobs: one on the main board for « all building blocks ... concernig digital processing », one inside each module driving the ladder. The conversion itself is the discrete ladder, not either FPGA.

device_settings.why: « The filters can be switched off for NOS operation. » Said by the maker, in a menu, with no condition. Without it the device « upsamples any material with a fixed rate of 16x » and decodes at 768 or 705.6 kHz through a 5k-tap Parks-McClellan filter of its own. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's stage belongs out of the path. This is also what makes correctable true: the field applies « only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM », and this is the first device in the catalogue whose maker offers NOS in so many words.

Three named variations: « linear, minimum and hybrid phase ». The maker describes each by its impulse response - linear splits « the ringing energy (Gibb's overshoot) ... equally split before and after impulse », minimum « shows all this energy after impulse », and the hybrid « exhibing very low overshoot before the impulse ». Hybrid is recorded as the setting because pre-ringing is the artefact apodising filters exist to remove. It applies only if NOS is NOT selected, which is the first ordered pair of settings in the catalogue.

DIGITAL INPUTS: « S/PDIF 24bit 44.1-192k PCM , DoP DSD64 »; « AES/EBU 24bit 44.1-192k PCM, DoP DSD64 »; « USB 32bit 44.1-384k PCM, DSD64-512 »; « HD-Link1 (LVDS) 32bit 44.1-384k PCM, DSD64-512 »; « HD-Link2 (LVDS) 32bit 44.1-384k PCM, DSD64-512 ». D/A CONVERSION: « For the effective D/A conversion stage we developed dedicated dac modules called RD-0 (used in Signature - 27 bit structure) and RD-1 (used in Edition - 26 bit structure). Modules themselves are complex pieces of technology, sharing a discrete sign-magnitude hybrid ladder topology, driven by a complex algorythm which is embedded into their own FPGA. »; « Currently RD-0/1 can sustain a maximum sample rate of 6 MHz, which is the industry's maximum sample rate specified for a audio dac. »; « The output of the dac modules is un-buffered ». SOFTWARE DEFINED ARCHITECTURE: « All building blocks of the Wavedream DAC concernig digital processing are built entirely on a single piece of programmable silicon - a FPGA. » CUSTOM DIGITAL FILTERS: « The Wavedream upsamples any material with a fixed rate of 16x. The dac modules will decode the digital stream with a rate of 768Khz, or 705.6Khz, respectively, according to input sample rate. »; « we have created a custom Parks-McClellan upsampling filter. There are three variations avaialble on current firmware: linear, minimumand hybrid phase. They are highly optimized filters, offering stunning performance with a large number of taps (5k), and they are different in regard of impulse response. »; « For the linear phase, the ringing energy (Gibb's overshoot) is equally split before and after impulse. Minimum phase type shows all this energy after impulse, while our special hyrid phase filter has a combined response between linear and minimum, exhibing very low overshoot before the impulse. » EXTRA MENU FEATURES: « The filter select feature - discussed above. The filters can be switched off for NOS operation. »; « The clock setting - there are 2 modes of the digital PLL response, stream and local. »; « Dither - to improve R2R ladder linearity, ultrasonic dither is applied on the last 4 bits from the digital 24-bit word. »; « The Wavedream has a 256 steps volume control which allows direct connection of a power amplifier. The volume control has 0.5 dB steps ». OUTPUT STAGE: « the output stage is totally discrete and acts as a high-speed buffer », « we combined j-fet & bipolar devices into a class A design ». data.chip: « Texas Instruments DAC8812C x 4 » with « proprietary Schiit time- and frequency-domain optimized digital filter implemented on Analog Devices SHARC DSP processor, running 8X oversampling ». The maker calls the whole arrangement « Schiit Multiform™ ».

device_settings.why: « choose a true non-oversampling mode (NOS) to bypass our digital filter entirely ». The maker's own words, and the word « entirely » is what makes correctable true: in NOS the 8X oversampling stage is out of the path, which is the precondition the field requires.

source.quote: Schiit Audio's own page for the Gungnir 2, read 2026-11-24. « Inputs: Coaxial SPDIF, Optical SPDIF, USB ». « Input Capability »: « Up to 32/384 for Unison 384 Up to 32/192 for other inputs ». data.chip: « a standard delta-sigma modulator, in this case an ES9028 » (ESS), with Schiit's own time- and frequency-domain optimised filter ahead of it.

device_settings.setting: Mesh or NOS filter mode switching
device_settings.why: The maker offers the choice in its « Forkbeard Capabilities » list. In Mesh mode Schiit's own filter runs; in NOS it does not. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's stage belongs out of the path - and NOS is the precondition `correctable` requires.

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.
data._corrected: This record was called "Yggdrasil" and carried a quote about ONE of its three variants. Schiit sells the Yggdrasil in three flavours on three different converters: the OG on Analog Devices AD5791 at 20 bits, Less is More on four TI DAC8812 at 16 bits, and More is Less on TI DAC11001 at 20 bits. Only the second is described here, and only the second is 16-bit - so the record's bits, its chip and its family were right for a device its own name did not identify. Renamed rather than generalised. The apparent contradiction between "16-bit TI DAC" and the ladder family was never one: all three are multibit ladder parts rather than delta-sigma, which is the whole point of Schiit's multibit line.
data.chip: Four TI DAC8812, 16-bit. The maker's multibit line uses ladder parts rather than delta-sigma; the other two Yggdrasil variants use Analog Devices AD5791 and TI DAC11001, both 20-bit.

device_settings.why: « all Yggdrasils also offer non-oversampling, or NOS, mode. » Stated of the whole line by the maker. In NOS the SHARC filter is out of the path, which is what makes correctable true.

data._corrected: Keyed and filed under Topping until 2026-11-20. There is no Topping D300: every search for one returns SMSL's, on the ROHM BD34301EKV - which is the very chip family this record already carried. The record's own evidence named SMSL twice and the brand field said Topping, and the contradiction sat in _verify from the moment brand and model were split apart. Splitting them is what made it visible at all; while the name was one string, "Topping D300" read as a single fact nobody could check.

data.device_settings: Filtre de conversion sur le reglage de frequence le plus bas.

open_doubt.text: The chip family holds - every source says AKM - but the quoted evidence may be about a different model: it cites the author's reserve about SMSL devices 'a puce 4499EX', while reviews of the D-6 describe two AK4493. Both are AKM parts, so the family and everything inherited from it stand; the specific DSD Direct reserve may not apply to this model.

source.quote: Soulution's own page for the 560, read 2026-11-24. Table headed « Bit depth/sampling rage max » (the misspelling is the page's): « AES/EBU: 24 bit/192 kHz »; « SPDIF: 24 bit/192 kHz »; « Optical: 24 bit/96 kHz »; « USB: 24 bit/384 kHz, 1 bit/5.64 MHz »; « Network: 24 bit/384 kHz, 1 bit/5.64 MHz ». open_doubt.text: Whether this device reconverts DSD to PCM. The temptation is strong and the page does not close it. « Audio data is buffered then upsampled to 24Bit/384kHz » describes the signal path with no exception; the inputs accept « 1 bit/5.64 MHz »; the output of that stage is stated as 24-bit PCM. Read together they say DSD arrives, meets a PCM upsampler and leaves as 24/384 - which would make dsd_reconverted_to_pcm true. But « Audio data » is the maker's word for everything it had been talking about, which was PCM, and the sentence never says the 1-bit stream takes that path. No fact is written. Getting this field wrong is expensive: it is what tells an engine whether sending DSD to this device is worth anything at all, and the cascade carries it almost everywhere: re-measured 2026-11-24, 56 of the 59 records that resolve it at all take it from their family, 3 from evidence of their own.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: One sentence from Soulution about what happens to a 1-bit input, or a manual. Failing that, a measurement: feed DSD128 and look for the PCM signature. Do NOT resolve it by reading the upsampling sentence harder.

data.chip: « der AKM AK4493 SEQ VELVETSOUND » (Asahi Kasei), inside a module SPL calls the « DAC768v2 ». The « 120V-Technologie » working at « +/-60 V » and the « SLP120 (Super Low-Pass) » filter are the ANALOGUE output stage and its reconstruction filter - SPL's whole selling point, and not the converter.

source.quote: SPL's own page for the Phonitor 3 DAC, read 2026-11-25. The page is German-only. On USB: « Ueber USB wandelt der Phonitor 3 DAC PCM-Audio-Signale mit einer Aufloesung von 32 Bit und einer Abtastrate von bis zu 768 kHz sowie DSD-Signale mit einer Aufloesung von bis zu DSD256. » On the S/PDIF coaxial and optical inputs and on AES/EBU, each described in its own sentence: « mit Abtastraten von bis zu 192 kHz und einer Wortbreite von 16 Bit bis 24 Bit empfangen » and, for AES/EBU, « maximalen Abtastrate von 192 kHz und einer Wortbreite von 16 Bit bis 24 Bit ». On the converter: « Als Wandler-Chip im Digital/Analog-Wandler des Phonitor 3 DAC kommt ... der DAC768v2 ... der AKM AK4493 SEQ VELVETSOUND(TM) ». On DSD in the DAC768v2 section: « Auch Direct Stream Digital wird bis zu einer Aufloesung von DSD4 bzw. DSD256 unterstuetzt. » On the analogue stage: « Die 120V-Technologie arbeitet mit +/-60 V » and an analogue reconstruction filter « SLP120 (Super Low-Pass) », « ein analogen 'Super Low-Pass'-Filter mit 120V-Technologie ». spl.audio has no prohibition: the Impressum and the AGB were both READ and neither restricts copying, reproduction or extraction; the only rights line is the footer « (c) 2026 SPL electronics GmbH ».

data._aliases_typed: Typed 2026-11-24. An untyped alias list merged three different things and one of them is dangerous: a SPELLING is the same object written differently, an EDITION is a variant of this model that no fact yet distinguishes, and a NEIGHBOUR is a DIFFERENT PRODUCT resolved here only because it has no record of its own. Before typing, a match on "Spring 2" would have asserted the Spring 3's facts for another generation, and "HA 200" - a headphone amplifier - sat beside the DAC 200 as if it were the same device. They are listed together because they share one USB identity. THE RELATIONS WERE ASSIGNED FROM PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE, NOT FROM A CITED SOURCE: a neighbour is the claim that two things are different devices, which deserves evidence like any other, and aliases live in identity where the evidence rule does not reach. Contest them.
data.chip: The maker's own discrete DSD stage, with no DSP in the DSD path. Not a commercial converter chip, and a case where an architecture family fits without inventing anything.
data.device_settings: Filtre analogique sur 60 kHz pour la bande la plus large.

device_settings.why: « UAC 1.0 / 2.0 (switchable) », and the input table rates the two as SEPARATE INTERFACES: UAC 2.0 takes 44.1-384 kHz and DSD, UAC 1.0 takes 44.1-48 kHz and no DSD at all. A factor of EIGHT on the rate, decided by a menu setting. UAC 1.0 exists for hosts with no driver; anything this engine runs on supports 2.0.

device_settings.set_to: F-8: Minimum Phase Slow Roll-Off Low Dispersion
device_settings.why: Eight filters, all named. F-8 is chosen: minimum phase has no pre-ringing, and the maker marks this one low-dispersion, which is the cost minimum phase otherwise pays. F-5 is the factory default and is linear phase, so leaving the device alone leaves pre-ringing in the path. Note F-2, « Linear Phase Fast Roll-Off Apodizing » - the third apodising filter found in this catalogue and the first offered as one of eight.

device_settings.why: Six named filters. F-6 is chosen: short delay is this maker's word for the minimum-phase family, which has no pre-ringing, and F-6 is the low-dispersion variant of it. F-3, the factory default, is also short delay but without the low-dispersion correction.

Two DSD filters, given as cut-off frequencies: « F-1 + DSD: 37kHz (Default) » and « F-2 + DSD: 65kHz ». The wider one is preferred for the same reason RME's « Wild Bandwidth » setting is preferred elsewhere in this catalogue: a DSD stream's noise is out of band, and a filter that cuts at 37 kHz is removing signal as well. BUT SEE THE CONSTRAINT BELOW - this setting is not always available.

« m-p: Preamp mode (volume adjustable) (Default) » against « m-d: DAC mode (volume not adjustable) ». DAC mode takes the volume control out of the path entirely, which is what you want when the device feeds an amplifier that has its own. First record in the catalogue where a setting removes the attenuator rather than improving it.

data.chip: No converter chip: « R2R DAC technology using 600 pieces of 0.01% VAR Bulk Metal Foil resistors Vishay Foil Resistors », « the famous naked Vishay foil ». The maker counts its resistors and names their tolerance and their supplier, which is more than any chip datasheet in this catalogue says about its own silicon - and still gives no ladder bit depth, the field that is known for 7 records of 61.

device_settings.why_it_matters: A filter the listener can switch off. Second such setting in this catalogue after RME's five DA filters, and the second argument that internal_bypass - which assumes a RATE threshold - is modelled for the rarer shape.

open_doubt.text: KEPT ON PURPOSE, against the move that took its two neighbours out. This record shares their identity - brand "unknown", model "unknown" - and it is not the same kind of thing. Its source says so: « Not a device. The record the engine uses when the driver reports an identity no record matches and the listener has not said. » It is the TERMINAL of the cascade, the bottom a consumer resolves to when nothing else matches, and deleting it would remove the floor rather than a duplicate. akm-generique and ess-generique were chip defaults wearing a device; this one is the absence of a device, which is a role no chip family can fill.
open_doubt.what_is_doubtful: Its `kind` says "dac", which is the one field that is plainly wrong: it is not a converter, it is the answer "we do not know which converter". And it carries dsd_direct false where its chip family says "unknown" - both end in the conservative branch, so nothing breaks, but two levels still disagree. The real question is whether a terminal belongs in devices/ at all, or whether a consumer should get it from the vocabulary instead of from a record that has to pretend to be a device to exist.

data.chip: No part number, and the maker goes out of its way not to give one: « a chosen DAC chip », corrected from outside by a « Dual-differential musIC 3 128-bit-feed-forward error correction process », with « Processing is done at 128 bit internal resolution ». So bought silicon, deliberately unnamed, with the maker's own correction ahead of it.

source.quote: Wadax's own page for the Atlantis Reference DAC, read 2026-11-24. Specification block, « Inputs: »: « USB (32-384KHz, 16-24-32 bits, DSD64, DSD128, DSD256, MQA) »; « 2xSPDIF RCA (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « 2xSPDIF BNC (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « 2xAES-EBU (32KHz-192KHz, 16-24 bits) »; « Native Reference Wadax Link (native PCM, DSD), 3xAES-EBU, 1 RJ45 »; « Optional: WADAX Akasa Optical Module ». On the processing: « By mapping the error mechanisms of a chosen DAC chip under load using Adaptive Delta Hilbert Mapping »; « Dual-differential musIC 3 128-bit-feed-forward error correction process »; « Processing is done at 128 bit internal resolution »; « Zepto Reference clock: doubled the master clock frequency with only 12fs total jitter. »; « including native DSD replay over our proprietary triple AES-EBU connection ». Self-description: « The Atlantis REFERENCE DAC is our response to these findings, with lower levels of clock noise and significant improvements in PSU and mechanical isolation. » and « The result is the most accurate and most musically satisfying DAC ever designed. » The page also carries spec images at images/dacConnectivity.png and images/dacInNumbers.png, not opened: the text above is the page's own.

open_doubt.text:
TWO DOUBTS, AND THE FIRST IS THE MOST VALUABLE QUESTION IN THIS CATALOGUE.
1. Weiss writes « The unit can also convert DSD audio to PCM and offers a digital output in AES/EBU format. » If that means DSD is re-converted internally before analogue conversion, dsd_reconverted_to_pcm is true and a consumer should never send this device DSD. If it means the unit can transcode DSD to PCM for its AES/EBU digital output, the field is untouched. The sentence supports both readings. One email to Weiss settles it - which is exactly the inlet this catalogue rates highest and has never used.
2. The ES9028PRO is stated for « the MK2 version » only. By this catalogue's own rule an edition becomes a record of its own the day a fact distinguishes it, and a different converter board is such a fact. So DAC204-MK2 has earned a record - the first alias typed `edition` to do so - and what the pre-MK2 used is unknown. Nine households own a « DAC204 » with no generation stated.
